intake.description.0.en: The purpose of the intake questionnaire is to learn a little more about each user.

intake.Q1.helpGroup.text.1.en: In order to examine the differences between genders.

intake.Q2.title.0.en: What is your date of birth (month and year)?

intake.Q2.helpGroup.text.1.en: In order to examine the differences between age groups.

intake.Q3.title.0.en: What is your postal code (place of residence)?

intake.Q3.helpGroup.text.1.en: In order to verify the representativeness of our cohort (the group of participants in this study) and to examine the geographical differences in the spread of the coronavirus and influenza.

intake.Q3.helpGroup.text.2.en: How should I answer this question?

intake.Q3.helpGroup.text.3.en: Insert the postal code of your place of residence

intake.Q3.rg.scg.option.1.en: I prefer not to answer this question

intake.Q3.error.3.en: Please enter the four digits of your postal code

intake.Q4.title.0.en: What is your current professional status?

intake.Q4.helpGroup.text.1.en: To check how representative our sample is compared to the population as a whole and to find out whether the chance of getting infected with the flu (Influenza) is different for people in different types of occupation.

intake.Q4.helpGroup.text.2.en: How should I answer this question?

intake.Q4.helpGroup.text.3.en: Please, tick the box that most precisely describes your main occupation. For pre-school children who don't go to daycare tick the "other" box.

intake.Q4b.title.0.en: What is the postal code of your school/college/workplace (where you spend the majority of your working/studying time)?

intake.Q4b.helpGroup.text.1.en: To be able to determine the distance you regularly travel during your daily movements.

intake.Q4b.rg.scg.option.2.en: Not applicable (e.g. I don’t have a fixed workplace)

intake.Q4b.error.3.en: Please enter the four digits of your postal code

intake.Q4b.error.4.en: Please enter at most four digits

intake.Q4h.title.0.en: Which of the following descriptions most closely describes your main occupation?

intake.Q4h.helpGroup.text.1.en: To check how representative our sample is compared to the population as a whole and to find out whether the chance of getting the flu (Influenza) is different for people in different types of occupation.

intake.Q4h.helpGroup.text.2.en: How should I answer this question?

intake.Q4h.helpGroup.text.3.en: Please tick the box that most closely describes your main occupation.

intake.Q4h.rg.scg.option.0.en: Services and Sales Workers (Personal Services Workers, Sales Workers, Personal Care Workers, Protective Services Workers)

intake.Q4h.rg.scg.option.1.en: Craft and related trades workers (Handicraft and printing workers, Food processing, wood working, garment and other craft and related trades workers,  Metal, machinery and related trades workers, Electrical and electronic trades workers, Building and related trades workers, excluding electricians)

intake.Q4h.rg.scg.option.2.en: Armed Forces Occupations (Commissioned armed forces officers; Armed forces occupations other ranks; Non-commissioned armed forces officers)

intake.Q4h.rg.scg.option.3.en: Managers (Chief Executives, Senior Officials and Legislators; Administrative and Commercial Managers; Production and Specialized Services Managers; Hospitality, Retail and Other Services Managers)

intake.Q4h.rg.scg.option.4.en: Professionals (Science and Engineering Professionals; Health Professional; Teaching Professionals; Business and Administration Professionals; Information and Communications Technology Professionals; Legal, Social and Cultural Professionals)

intake.Q4h.rg.scg.option.5.en: Technicians and Associate Professionals (Science and Engineering Associate Professionals; Health Associate Professionals; Business and Administration Associate Professionals; Legal, Social, Cultural and Related Associate Professionals; Information and Communications Technicians)

intake.Q4h.rg.scg.option.6.en: Clerical Support Workers (General and Keyboard Clerks; Customer Services Clerks;  Numerical and Material Recording Clerks; Other Clerical Support Workers)

intake.Q4h.rg.scg.option.7.en: Skilled Agricultural, Forestry and Fishery Workers

intake.Q4h.rg.scg.option.8.en: Plant and Machine Operators and Assemblers (Stationary Plant and Machine Operators; Assemblers; Drivers and Mobile Plant Operators)

intake.Q4h.rg.scg.option.9.en: Elementary Occupations (Cleaners and Helpers; Agricultural, Forestry and Fishery Labourers; Labourers in Mining, Construction, Manufacturing and Transport; Food Preparation Assistants; Street and Related Sales and Services Workers; Refuse Workers and Other Elementary Workers)

intake.Q4d.title.0.en: What is the highest level of formal education/qualification that you have?

intake.Q4d.helpGroup.text.1.en: To check how representative our sample is compared to the population as a whole of other countries like the UK (Italy, Belgium..).

intake.Q4d.helpGroup.text.2.en: How should I answer this question?

intake.Q4d.helpGroup.text.3.en: Please choose the box that represents your HIGHEST academic/educational level/qualification. The different option rougly correspond to: 1 - no qualifications, 2 - school - leaving school at around 16 years of age, 3 - school - leaving school at around 18 years of age, 4 - University degree or equivalent professional qualification (Bachelor Degree etc.), 5 - Higher degree or advanced professional qualification (Master Degree, PhD etc.). If you are an adult who is currently undergoing part - time training (e.g.night school) then tick the box that represents your current highest level of education.

intake.Q4d.rg.mcg.option.2.en: High School Diploma (Matura, Technical Matura or equivalent) or Apprenticeship

intake.Q4d.rg.mcg.option.4.en: Higher Degree or equivalent (e.g. Masters Degree, PGCE, PhD, Medical Doctorate, Advanced Professional Award)

intake.Q5.title.0.en: Except people you meet on public transportation, do you have contact with any of the following people during the course of a typical day (presumed no COVID-19 measures are in place)?

intake.Q5.helpGroup.text.1.en: To determine whether you are likely to be exposed to a higher infection risk than the average person (e.g. work with children, or patients).

intake.Q5.helpGroup.text.3.en: Such groups of people include any setting where one comes into contact with larger numbers of people at once, e.g. a teacher who may be in contact with many children during a day.

intake.Q5.rg.mcg.option.0.en: More than 10 children or teenagers (without counting your own children)

intake.Q5.rg.mcg.option.1.en: More than 10 people over 65 years of age

intake.Q5.rg.mcg.option.3.en: Groups of people (more than 10 individuals at any one time)

intake.Q6.title.0.en: INCLUDING YOU, how many people in each of the following age groups live in your household?

intake.Q6.helpGroup.text.1.en: Members of larger households, or people living with children, are exposed to a higher infection risk than others.

intake.Q6c.title.0.en: Is one or several of these people at risk of complications in case of the flu (influenza) or COVID-19 (e.g, pregnant, over 65, underlying health condition, obese, etc.)?

intake.Q6c.helpGroup.text.2.en: How should I answer this question?

intake.Q6c.rg.scg.option.2.en: I don't know/I would rather not answer

intake.Q6b.title.0.en: How many of the children in your household attend school or day-care?

intake.Q6b.helpGroup.text.1.en: Attending school, daycare or childcare can increase the risk of contracting the coronavirus or influenza, as well as other similar illnesses. We wish to study this issue.

intake.Q6b.helpGroup.text.2.en: How should I answer this question?

intake.Q6b.helpGroup.text.3.en: If your child attends school, daycare or childcare (even if only one day a week), please count it. Participation in (sport) associations or other extracurricular activities does not count.

intake.Q7.title.0.en: What means of transportation do you typically use for your daily activities?

intake.Q7.helpGroup.text.1.en: We want to investigate whether people who regularly use public transportation have a higher risk of infection.

intake.Q7.helpGroup.text.2.en: How should I answer this question?

intake.Q7.helpGroup.text.3.en: Check the box that best matches the means of transportation you most frequently use.

intake.Q7.rg.9JtQ.text.0.en: Please select the transportation means you use the most.

intake.Q8.title.0.en: How often do you suffer from common colds or flu-like illnesses?

intake.Q8.helpGroup.text.1.en: We want to know if certain people have an increased risk of infection.

intake.Q11.title.0.en: Do you take regular medication for any of the following medical conditions?

intake.Q11.helpGroup.text.1.en: This question allows us to investigate whether you have other/underlying medical conditions that may increase your risk of suffering a more severe illness if you are infected.

intake.Q11.helpGroup.text.3.en: Only answer "yes" if you take regular medication to treat your medical problem. If, for instance, you only occasionally use an asthma inhaler, then do not answer "yes" for asthma.

intake.Q11.rg.mcg.option.3.en: Chronic lung disorders besides asthma e.g. COPD, emphysema, or other disorders that affect your breathing

intake.Q11.rg.mcg.option.6.en: An immunocompromising condition (e.g. splenectomy, organ transplant, acquired immune deficiency, cancer treatment)

intake.Q12.helpGroup.text.1.en: Pregnancy is a potential risk factor for severe symptoms in the event of infection with influenza or COVID-19.

intake.Q12.rg.scg.option.2.en: I don't know/I would rather not answer

intake.Q12b.title.0.en: What trimester of the pregnancy are you in?

intake.Q12b.helpGroup.text.1.en: The risk of severe symptoms can vary depending on the trimester of the pregnancy. Still, this link has not yet been clearly established.

intake.Q12b.rg.scg.option.3.en: I don't know/I would rather not answer

intake.Q13.helpGroup.text.1.en: Smoking might make you more likely to get a more severe dose of virus (viral load). We would like to test this.

intake.Q13.helpGroup.text.3.en: Please, answer as accurately as possible.

intake.Q13.rg.scg.option.2.en: Yes, daily - fewer than 10 cigarettes per day

intake.Q13.rg.scg.option.3.en: Yes, daily - 10 or more cigarettes per day

intake.Q13.rg.scg.option.5.en: I dont know/I would rather not answer

intake.Q14.title.0.en: Do you have one of the following allergies that can cause respiratory symptoms?

intake.Q14.helpGroup.text.1.en: Certain allergies provoke the same/similar symptoms as respiratory infections.

intake.Q14.helpGroup.text.2.en: How should I answer this question?

intake.Q14.helpGroup.text.3.en: Multiple answers are possible, check all that apply.

intake.Q14.rg.mcg.option.2.en: Allergy against domestic animals or pets

intake.Q14.rg.mcg.option.3.en: Other allergies that cause respiratory symptoms (e.g. sneezing, runny eyes)

intake.Q14.rg.mcg.option.4.en: I do not have an allergy that causes respiratory symptoms

intake.Q15.title.0.en: Do you follow a special diet?

intake.Q26.title.0.en: Are you taking or do you plan to take this winter homeopathic products in order to prevent COVID-19?

intake.Q26.helpGroup.text.1.en: We are interested to know more about your health-related habits

intake.Q17.title.0.en: Where did you first hear about this platform?

intake.Q17.helpGroup.text.1.en: We would like to know how you found out about our website.

intake.Q17.rg.mcg.option.1.en: In the newspaper or in a magazine

intake.Q17.rg.mcg.option.2.en: The internet (a website, link, a search engine)

intake.surveyEnd.title.0.en: Thank you! This was all for now, please submit (push « send ») your responses. Please come back or continue reporting symptoms you experienced during the last week.
